derivation: Key is the Swift interpolation "\(senderID)-\(timestamp)-\(type)-\(digestPrefix)" where senderID is PeerID(hexData:) rendered lowercase hex, type is the UInt8 in decimal, and digestPrefix is sha256(payload).prefix(4) in lowercase hex. Digests computed with python hashlib.

vectors.name: same_sender_ts_type_other_payload
vectors.note: PRIORITY: identical sender, timestamp and type; only the payload differs. Without the SHA-256 prefix in the key these collapse, and the post-handshake flush (message + delivered + read inside one millisecond) loses every packet after the first.

vectors.name: delivered_receipt_same_millisecond
vectors.note: The sibling packet from that same flush: same sender and millisecond, different type and payload.

vectors.name: read_receipt_same_millisecond
vectors.note: And the third: same type as the previous one, so only the payload digest separates them.

vectors.name: empty_payload
vectors.note: SHA-256 of the empty string still yields a 4-byte prefix.
